## Problem

On 2026-08-31 (~17:30-18:00 PDT), three consecutive MCP log_session writes failed with: flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: host=boot-bf4c34b1-475c-4363-8ff6-aada80c3c3ab pid=49003 start=19655570 held=155-174s pid_state=live op=compact-sweep).

## Executed evidence (all captured during the incident)

- ps -p 49003 returns nothing (rc=1) - the pid does not exist on this host.
- lsof on /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock shows NO holder (rc=1); the file is the 0-byte flock target.
- held values across the three attempts were non-monotonic (158s, 155s, 174s) while start stayed constant - consistent with a stale stamp being re-read, not a live re-acquiring sweep.
- Discriminator: an immediate local-CLI write (rebar session-log append) from the main checkout succeeded instantly (log heinous-undivining-ungulate / 0a3b-4201-6528-4f30), proving the store lock itself was free.

## Hypothesis (mechanism to confirm at RCA)

The MCP server's lock acquisition reads a holder stamp naming a dead pid and its liveness check judges it live (macOS pid-reuse or kill(pid,0) semantics; the larval-tribal-tigermoth class - stale lock unbounded without /proc), so every MCP write waits the full 181s and fails while the underlying flock is uncontended. Possibly interacting with the MCP server's own tracker path/clone rather than the shared checkout (the local CLI on the same store did not see the holder). The compact-sweep at pid 49003 exited without its stamp being cleared.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause confirmed by reproduction: which lock/stamp the MCP server path reads, and why pid_state reported live for a dead pid.
- [ ] A dead-holder stamp can no longer wedge MCP writes for the full timeout: liveness verification cannot return live for a nonexistent pid (or the stamp is advisory and the kernel flock is authoritative).
- [ ] Regression test covering the dead-pid-stamp case on the MCP write path.

## Phase 1 RCA (2026-08-31)

Step 0(a): duplicate sweep ran `rebar search "dead compact-sweep holder pid_state live"` and `rebar list --type bug --status open,in_progress`; only this bug matches the MCP stale compact-sweep holder. The open session-log ticket `heinous-undivining-ungulate` is the incident log/discovered_from parent, not a duplicate. Closed sibling `larval-tribal-tigermoth` is same stale-pid lock class and prior-art fix pattern.

Step 0(b): no version field exists; report has incident time 2026-08-31 and created_at `1788228927503392001`, so the floor is newest origin/main at or before that timestamp: `779449bd19fb96d072af58b624b9a5fa0f3b04ee`. `git log <floor>..origin/main -- src/rebar/_store/lock.py src/rebar/_store/sync.py src/rebar/_ref_lock.py src/rebar/_heartbeat.py` found no suspect-path changes after the floor.

Step 0(c): fresh worktree `/Users/joeoakhart/storelock-fix` is current at `1299d9deb6da82708bf694e19572ef8579664f34` (= origin/main).

Confirmed mechanism: MCP `log_session` calls `rebar.append_session_log` from `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:342-356`, then the shared append path takes `rebar._store.lock.write_lock` (`src/rebar/_commands/session_log.py:157-205`, `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`). Lock acquisition takes the kernel `.ticket-write.lock` first, then the mkdir stamp dir `.ticket-write.lock.d`; if mkdir remains present until deadline it raises `LockTimeout(..., describe_lock_holder(tracker))` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py:482-501`). The holder text is read from `.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py:273-322`) and rendered via `_describe_stamped_pid` (`src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py:228-248`).

Runtime proof: in an isolated scratch repo I forged `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` as `rebar-lock v2 host=<this host> ns=- pid=49003 start=- op=compact-sweep`, proved the kernel flock file was free by taking `fcntl.LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`, then drove the real in-process MCP `log_session` tool. I instrumented only the liveness seams: `_acquire_fcntl` returned a live fd (`fcntl_acquired=True`), `_pid_alive(49003)` returned True, and `_process_start_time(49003)` returned None. The MCP tool then failed through the real path with `flock: could not acquire lock after 1s (holder: ... pid_state=live op=compact-sweep)`, while the mkdir dir remained. That discriminates the bug from true kernel-flock contention: the kernel leg was free and held by the waiter; the stale mkdir owner stamp alone caused the timeout.

Production-path discriminator: an actual `rebar-log_session` MCP call in this session timed out with `-32001`, while a local CLI `rebar session-log append "local CLI smoke after MCP timeout for avoided-flannel-eeve"` in this worktree succeeded instantly, creating `oxymoronic-ammonic-bats` (`f199-88ee-de0d-4a37`). The shared checkout path `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker` had no `.ticket-write.lock.d` at that moment and `lsof` showed no holder for `.ticket-write.lock`. Therefore the active MCP server is operating on a different tracker clone/path than the local worktree/shared checkout; the local checkout cannot clear the MCP server's private stale mkdir stamp.

Why `pid_state=live` for a dead original holder: `_describe_stamped_pid` currently reports `live` from bare `_pid_alive(pid)` whenever host and pid namespace are comparable; it does not qualify the pid-number probe with the stamped/current start time. On macOS/no-`/proc`, `_process_start_time` is unavailable, so a pid-number reuse (or a different MCP host where pid 49003 exists) is rendered as `pid_state=live` even though it does not prove the stamped compact-sweep owner still exists. The stale adjudicator has the same gap for fresh stamps: `_stamp_is_stale` treats current_start=None as refuse-without-proof and, after larval-tribal-tigermoth, only reclaims past the 1h ceiling. For MCP writes with a 60s/181s acquisition budget, that means a fresh stale mkdir stamp still wedges every write for the full request timeout despite the authoritative kernel fcntl leg being free.

Defect legitimacy: defect. The shared lock contract documented in `_acquire_mkdir` says this code is reached only after the waiter holds the exclusive fcntl leg on the same tracker; for same-host v2 stamps, a live owner would still hold that kernel lock, so the kernel flock being free is positive proof the mkdir stamp is orphaned. The incident violates the write-lock contract that a dead-holder stamp must not discard writes while the kernel lock is uncontended, and is the same stale-pid class previously fixed by `larval-tribal-tigermoth`.

Attribution: caused_by `larval-tribal-tigermoth` (`ab00-1407-2da3-42fd`) as a plan-defect/omission, not a line-introducing regression. Its own close comment says immediate reclaim based on `fcntl_held` was considered safe but deliberately NOT done, leaving it for follow-up; this MCP incident proves that deferred case is required because the 1h ceiling exceeds MCP/write request budgets. I will pass `--caused-by=larval-tribal-tigermoth` on close.

## Fix plan

Acceptance criteria for the fix:

- [ ] Through the MCP write surface, a same-host v2 mkdir owner stamp whose pid probe is unqualified (`_pid_alive` true but `_process_start_time` unavailable/different from the stamped owner) is treated as stale once the waiter has acquired the kernel fcntl leg, so a stale compact-sweep mkdir stamp cannot burn the full write timeout while `.ticket-write.lock` is free.
- [ ] Holder diagnostics no longer render an unqualified pid-number match as `pid_state=live`; they report the pid as unverified/unprobeable (or recycled/not-owner when start times differ) unless the current process start time corroborates the stamp.
- [ ] Regression coverage includes the real MCP `log_session` path with a forged dead compact-sweep owner stamp and proves the kernel fcntl leg was acquired before reclaim; the test is RED on current main because the tool times out on the mkdir stamp.
- [ ] Existing lock-age and recycled-pid tests remain green: corroborated-live owners are never broken on a timer, fresh foreign-host stamps stay refused, and aged unprovable stamps remain bounded.
- [ ] Step-7 parity census covers CLI, MCP/API, library facade, automated callers (sync/reconciler/ref-lock/heartbeat), and dual-direction diagnostics for the same invariant.

Implementation outline: update `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` only, inside the shared owner-stamp decision table and diagnostic renderer. In `_stamp_is_stale`, for same-host/same-namespace v2 stamps where `_pid_alive(pid)` is true but `current_start is None`, return `fcntl_held or _mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling(artifact_path)` instead of waiting solely for the ceiling; if current start is known and differs from stamped start, keep reclaiming immediately. In `_describe_stamped_pid`, qualify live by start-time corroboration: dead -> `not-running`, known differing start -> `not-owner (recycled pid)`, unknown current start -> `unverified-live (start unknown)`/equivalent, known matching start -> `live`. No new dependency and no MCP-core edits.
